findings.claim: Only the first half of TRUNK-6701's 'Requested change' is implemented - the unused unique-id request attribute is neither removed nor made lazy - and the ticket is now Closed with nothing on the record that removing it would actually break downstream modules.
findings.evidence: JIRA TRUNK-6701 (fetched via https://openmrs.atlassian.net/rest/api/2/issue/TRUNK-6701) says verbatim: 'Only write session attributes when their values actually change, and remove (or make lazy) the unused unique-id attribute'; status is Closed, and ibacher's ticket comment records the merge plus 2.9.x/2.8.x/2.7.x backports. In the head worktree at d381957e, `git grep -n INIT_REQ_UNIQUE_ID` returns exactly two hits, web/src/main/java/org/openmrs/web/WebConstants.java:20 (the declaration) and web/src/main/java/org/openmrs/web/filter/OpenmrsFilter.java:64 (the write) - i.e. nothing in core reads it, as the ticket claims. Positive control for that search: `git grep -c doFilterInternal` on the same file returns 2. Outside core it IS read: `gh api search/code -f q='INIT_REQ_UNIQUE_ID org:openmrs'` returns total_count 10 across openmrs-core, openmrs-module-legacyui (HtmlIncludeTag, PortletController, PortletControllerTest), openmrs-module-reporting, openmrs-module-htmlformflowsheet, openmrs-module-htmlwidgets, openmrs-module-personalhr, openmrs-module-uiframework. I fetched legacyui at sha da89912c82ecc7f52e74c66fbfd779000c933414: omod/src/main/java/org/openmrs/web/controller/PortletController.java:111-113 reads `String uniqueRequestId = (String) request.getAttribute(WebConstants.INIT_REQ_UNIQUE_ID);` and then calls `uniqueRequestId.equals(lastRequestId)` with no null guard, so deleting line 64 NPEs every portlet render; omod/src/main/java/org/openmrs/web/taglib/HtmlIncludeTag.java:158-171 logs an error and degrades its include-dedup to "". Positive controls on both fetches: the files came back 428 and 258 lines respectively (an earlier raw.githubusercontent fetch of the same paths returned 0 lines and 0 matches for the control string 'class', which is how I caught that the first fetch had failed). The PR is right not to remove it; what is missing is that the ticket was closed as if it had been done. Ask: either add the lazy variant, or say on TRUNK-6701 that removal is unsafe, so nobody 'finishes' the ticket later by deleting line 64. The existing one-line comment 'used by htmlInclude tag' is the only thing standing between that attribute and a future cleanup PR.

findings.claim: The new dataset is a third verbatim copy of a <users> row that already ships on the web test classpath, and no new user is needed at all - the base test class already authenticates the thread as `admin` before every test.
findings.evidence: The row at web/src/test/resources/OpenmrsFilterTest-initial.xml:15 is byte-identical (same user_id 5506, same password/salt, same uuid 06d05314-e132-11de-babe-001e37123456) to api/src/test/resources/org/openmrs/api/include/AdministrationServiceTest-globalproperties.xml:27 and api/src/test/resources/org/openmrs/api/include/EncounterServiceTest-initialData.xml:95 - confirmed with `git grep -rn 06d05314-e132-11de-babe-001e37123456`, which returns exactly those three hits. Those api resources are already on the web test classpath: web/pom.xml:41-47 declares `org.openmrs.api:openmrs-api:test-jar` under the comment 'Test-jar for sharing api test resources in web tests', and the sibling test in the very same package, web/src/test/java/org/openmrs/web/filter/update/UpdateFilterTest.java:45, does `executeDataSet("org/openmrs/api/include/UserServiceTest.xml")` rather than adding its own copy. Simpler still: api/src/test/java/org/openmrs/test/jupiter/BaseContextSensitiveNonTransactionalTest.java:386-388 has `protected Credentials getCredentials() { return new UsernamePasswordCredentials("admin", "test"); }`, and its @BeforeEach `baseSetupWithStandardDataAndAuthentication()` (lines 937-966) calls `authenticate()` for every context-sensitive test; the admin row with username="admin" is loaded from api/src/test/resources/org/openmrs/include/initialInMemoryTestDataSet.xml:18. So OpenmrsFilterTest.java:123-124 and :153-154 (`executeDataSet(FILTER_INITIAL_DATA_XML)` + `Context.authenticate(getTestUserCredentials())`), the private getTestUserCredentials() at :222, and the whole XML file can go, with the assertions changed from is("test_user") to is("admin") - or keep an explicit authenticate and use the inherited getCredentials(). Cost of what is there: a third copy of the same fixture row to keep in sync, plus an extra dataset load per authenticated test, in a module whose pom exists precisely so api fixtures need not be copied. I verified placement is NOT itself a problem: web/src/test/resources already holds root-level resources (AltAuthSchemeTestingApplicationContext.xml, log4j2.xml), so there is precedent for that, even though the parent pom's maven-jar-plugin config means openmrs-web publishes a -tests.jar (historical openmrs-web-*-tests.jar artifacts are present in ~/.m2).

findings.claim: The @AfterEach logout() can never execute its body in this class, and it duplicates a guarded logout the base class already performs.
findings.evidence: Deterministic chain, read end to end at d381957e: every test in the class calls doFilterInternal, whose finally block at web/src/main/java/org/openmrs/web/filter/OpenmrsFilter.java:114-116 runs `Context.clearUserContext()`; api/src/main/java/org/openmrs/api/context/Context.java:242-246 implements that as `userContextHolder.remove()` on a plain `ThreadLocal<Object[]>` declared at Context.java:145 (no initialValue override); Context.java:970-972 defines `isSessionOpen()` as `userContextHolder.get() != null`; and Context.java:713-716 opens logout() with `if (!isSessionOpen()) { return; }`. Nothing in any of the five tests re-sets the holder between the filter call and teardown, so OpenmrsFilterTest.java:54-57 always early-returns. Separately, api/src/test/java/org/openmrs/test/jupiter/BaseContextSensitiveNonTransactionalTest.java:992-1000 (`clearSessionAfterEachTest`) already runs `if (Context.isSessionOpen()) Context.logout();`, so even when it could fire it would be redundant. No behavioural harm - the next test's @BeforeEach reopens the session and re-authenticates - but the method reads as cleanup that is not happening. Deleting it is the fix.

findings.claim: The rewritten line still spells the session key as the bare literal "locale" even though this module already exports a constant for it, on a key that two other filters in the same package write a different type into.
findings.evidence: web/src/main/java/org/openmrs/web/filter/util/FilterUtil.java:36 declares `public static final String LOCALE_ATTRIBUTE = "locale";`, and it is used through that constant everywhere else in web/src/main - InitializationFilter.java:228, :445-447, :493-495, :988-995, :1019-1021 and UpdateFilter.java:129, plus StartupFilter.java:261. Those filters store a String there (InitializationFilter.java:1019 writes `locale.toString()`; the tests at web/src/test/java/org/openmrs/web/filter/update/UpdateFilterE2ETest.java:101 and initialization/InitializationFilterE2ETest.java:109 use "en"/"fr"), while OpenmrsFilter writes a java.util.Locale object. I checked and this is not a regression: the new `Objects.equals(session.getAttribute(name), value)` comparison is always false across those two types, so the write still happens exactly as before - but the new code's correctness now quietly depends on that, which is the reason the literal is worth replacing with FilterUtil.LOCALE_ATTRIBUTE. The literal itself is pre-existing; the PR rewrote the line, which is why it is worth a word. Type divergence on the key is out of scope for this PR.

dimensions_swept.solution fit: Read TRUNK-6701 in full via the Atlassian REST API (summary, description, status, comments). Its three acceptance criteria are all met: same end values for anonymous and authenticated requests, no writes when unchanged, tests for both user states. I traced each of the four original behaviour paths through the rewrite and confirmed the end state is identical: (a) userContext==null - the old code never called getAuthenticatedUser() on the freshly created context, the new code does, and UserContext.java:69 initialises `private User user = null` with the constructor at :105-107 setting only the auth scheme, so it returns null and the username stays anonymous; (b) userContext!=null with user==null - both reset to anonymous; (c) userContext!=null with user!=null - old wrote anonymous then the real name (2 writes), new writes the real name once; (d) user!=null with a null getUsername() - both end with the attribute removed, since setAttribute(name,null) is removeAttribute per the servlet spec and Objects.equals(null,null) short-circuits the no-op case. Session creation (httpRequest.getSession() at line 61) is untouched, which the ticket required. The one gap is the ticket's second requested change, AM1. Alternatives a maintainer here would weigh: (i) keep the unconditional writes and accept the churn - rejected, that is the bug; (ii) wrap the session in a dirty-tracking HttpSessionWrapper - a much larger change for two attributes, disproportionate; (iii) move the username/locale writes into the login/logout path so they are written once per authentication rather than tested per request - genuinely the smallest steady-state cost, but it would move behaviour out of the filter that uncaughtexception.jsp's copied logic and the servlet container both depend on, and it changes more than the ticket asked; (iv) what was done, a read-compare-write helper - proportionate, local, and behaviour-preserving. I agree with the approach chosen and say nothing about it.
dimensions_swept.correctness: The rewrite is behaviour-preserving on every path (enumerated under solution fit). I checked the concurrency angle (two parallel requests on one session now both read-then-maybe-write instead of both writing; end state identical, no new race), the invalidated-session angle (the added getAttribute throws IllegalStateException on the same sessions setAttribute already did, and line 61's getSession() has just produced a live session), and the logout-mid-request angle (both old and new code only reflect a logout on the following request). I also chased and then killed a candidate finding: that skipping the per-request locale write could stop a mutated-in-place UserContext from being flushed by a replicating session manager. It cannot, because UserContext is not actually serializable - api/src/main/java/org/openmrs/api/context/UserContext.java:50 declares `implements Serializable` but line 97 holds `private final AuthenticationScheme authenticationScheme`, and AuthenticationScheme.java:17, DaoAuthenticationScheme.java:20 and UsernamePasswordAuthenticationScheme.java:21 show none of that hierarchy implements Serializable. No blocking finding.
dimensions_swept.test coverage: Ran the falsification experiment rather than eyeballing it. `mvn -o -pl web test -Dtest=OpenmrsFilterTest` at d381957e: Tests run 5, Failures 0. I then replaced only web/src/main/java/org/openmrs/web/filter/OpenmrsFilter.java with `git show eda229b12a28a41ba35ecd75b910803da93631a8:` of the same path and re-ran: Tests run 5, Failures 3 - doFilterInternal_shouldNotRewriteUnchangedAnonymousSessionAttributes:113 expected <0> but was <1>, doFilterInternal_shouldNotRewriteUnchangedAuthenticatedSessionAttributes:181 expected <0> but was <2>, doFilterInternal_shouldSetAuthenticatedUsernameAndLocale:143 expected <1> but was <2>. So three of the five tests genuinely fail on base and pass on the head, and they assert the runtime effect (write counts on a recording session), not a proxy. File restored with `git checkout --`. The other two tests are characterisation tests that pass on base; that is fine. The anonymous-to-authenticated transition within one session is not tested directly, but it is the same code path as doFilterInternal_shouldUpdateChangedSessionAttributes (changed value produces exactly one write), so I did not raise it. Findings AM2 and AM3 are about how the tests are set up, not about what they prove.
dimensions_swept.security: No new surface. The change writes the same two session attributes to the same keys with the same values; nothing is newly exposed to the servlet container or to JSPs. No authorization check was added, moved or removed - Context.setUserContext/clearUserContext bracketing of chain.doFilter is untouched. The new fixture adds a test-only user whose password hash and salt are already committed twice elsewhere in the repo (identical to the admin row's), so no secret enters the diff that was not already there. The recording session subclass is test scope only. Nothing in the diff touches CSRF handling (the csrfguard cache-header block below is unchanged) or CI config.
dimensions_swept.performance: This is the PR's purpose and it holds. Per request the filter now performs two HttpSession.getAttribute reads (a map lookup on StandardSession) and, in the steady state, zero setAttribute calls, replacing one to three unconditional setAttribute calls. setAttribute is the more expensive side: it fires HttpSessionBindingListener/HttpSessionAttributeListener callbacks and, under a clustered manager, records a replication delta. I checked that core registers no HttpSessionAttributeListener - web/src/main/java/org/openmrs/web/Listener.java is the only session listener in the tree and it implements HttpSessionListener only (created/destroyed, lines 78, 153, 166). Nothing was added to a loop, no query was introduced, and UserContext.getLocale() (which can fall back to LocaleUtility.getDefaultLocale()) is called exactly once per request as before. No measurement was needed because the win is structural - strictly fewer writes, two cheap reads added.
dimensions_swept.project conventions: The test mirrors the shape of the package's existing filter tests (same package, BaseWebContextSensitiveTest, doFilterInternal_should* naming, @see javadoc on each test), and the context-sensitive base class is genuinely required rather than over-heavy, because the anonymous path calls Context.getAuthenticationScheme() which resolves a bean from the running application context (Context.java:195-207). The jspecify @NonNull import is consistent with existing usage - eight other files already import org.jspecify, including web/src/main/java/org/openmrs/web/filter/GZIPFilter.java in the same package. `git diff --stat --ignore-all-space` over the PR range returns the identical 3 files / +279 / -12, so there is no whitespace churn and no drive-by edits; every hunk is required by the ticket. The two convention items worth raising are AM2 (fixture duplication against the module's own api-test-jar sharing convention and its sibling UpdateFilterTest) and AM4 (the FilterUtil.LOCALE_ATTRIBUTE constant).

notes: Merge verdict: nothing blocking. The rewrite is behaviour-preserving on all four original paths, the tests genuinely fail on base and pass on the head, and the approach is the proportionate one. Everything I raise is a suggestion or a nit, and AM1 is the only one with lasting value - the ticket's second requested change (remove or lazify INIT_REQ_UNIQUE_ID) was silently dropped, and my verification shows dropping it was the right call because five OpenMRS modules read that request attribute and legacyui's PortletController would NPE on it, so the useful action is to record that on TRUNK-6701 rather than to change this PR. Process notes: (a) one candidate finding was killed by the skill's 'hunt for the fact that refutes your own claim' rule - the session-replication concern died once I read UserContext's non-serializable AuthenticationScheme field; (b) a second candidate (root-of-tests-jar placement for the new XML) died on the project's own precedent, since log4j2.xml and AltAuthSchemeTestingApplicationContext.xml already sit at that same root; (c) a third candidate (the test should be a plain unit test rather than a DB-backed context-sensitive one) died once I read Context.getAuthenticationScheme, which needs the running application context on the anonymous path; (d) an early curl of the legacyui sources silently returned nothing and would have produced a false absence claim, caught only by the positive control the skill mandates. Convergence: pass 1 produced AM1, pass 2 produced AM2/AM3/AM4, pass 3 produced nothing substantive (both of its candidates were refuted), so the sweep is closed. Worktree left clean at d381957e - `git status --porcelain` empty, the temporarily swapped OpenmrsFilter.java restored with `git checkout --`, no probe classes created, nothing written to GitHub.
